---
title: "Wait for it: eventReactive()"
subtitle: "Deciding when the app reacts"
---

With `reactive()`, the app reacts **immediately** to every change. That is not always what we want:

- the user must set **several options** before the result makes sense (choose a file, *then* the separator, *then* the variables…)
- the computation is **slow**, and we do not want it to start at every click on a menu

We want the app to wait until the user says **"go"**. The "go" is an `actionButton()`, and the waiting is done by `eventReactive()`.

## The two pieces

```r
# ui.R
actionButton("load", "Select dataset")                # <1>
```
1. A button with ID `load`. Remember: `input$load` is a counter that increases at every click

```r
# server.R
dataInput <- eventReactive(input$load, {              # <1>
  if (input$dataset == 1) {                           # <2>
    rock
  } else if (input$dataset == 2) {
    pressure
  } else {
    cars
  }
})
```
1. The **first argument is the trigger**: the code runs only when `input$load` changes, i.e., when the button is clicked
2. The code to run. It reads `input$dataset`, but changing the dataset **does not** trigger it: its value is simply read at the moment of the click

`dataInput()` is then used exactly as a `reactive()`: `data <- dataInput()` inside the `render*()` functions.

## The app

Change the dataset: nothing happens. Click the button: now it does.

```{shinylive-r}

{{< include ../apps/04-eventreactive/ui.R >}}
## file: server.R
{{< include ../apps/04-eventreactive/server.R >}}
```

Notice also that **before the first click the outputs are empty**: at the start the button has never been clicked, so `eventReactive()` has no value yet, and the outputs that need it wait silently.

## `reactive()` vs `eventReactive()`

| | `reactive()` | `eventReactive()` |
|---|---|---|
| Re-runs when… | **any** input it reads changes | **only** the trigger changes (e.g., a button) |
| Inputs read inside | are triggers | are only read, at the moment of the trigger |
| At the start | runs as soon as an output needs it | waits for the first trigger |
| You use it with | `dataInput()` | `dataInput()` |

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    D0["input$dataset"] -.->|"read only"| E["dataInput()<br/>eventReactive"]
    B["input$load<br/>(button)"] ==>|"trigger"| E
    E --> G["output$graph"]
    E --> S["output$summary"]
    style D0 fill:#2b6c8e,color:#fff
    style B fill:#d9534f,color:#fff
    style E fill:#f0ad4e,color:#fff
    style G fill:#8fd36f,color:#fff
    style S fill:#8fd36f,color:#fff
```

::: {.callout-note}
## And `observeEvent()`?

You will also find `observeEvent(input$button, { ... })`. It looks the same, but it **returns nothing**: it is used to *do* something (update a menu, show a message, save a file), not to *compute a value* to use in the outputs. To compute data for the outputs, use `eventReactive()`. There is an example in [Going further](../extras/update-inputs.qmd).
:::

Starting from your `reactive()` version of the app:

1. add an `actionButton("load", "Select dataset")` in the `sidebarPanel()`
2. turn `reactive({ ... })` into `eventReactive(input$load, { ... })`

Run the app and check that nothing happens until you click.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 1

See [`apps/04-eventreactive`](https://github.com/ottaviae/stat-shiny/tree/main/apps/04-eventreactive). Only two lines change compared to the `reactive()` version:

```r
# ui.R
actionButton("load", "Select dataset")
```

```r
# server.R
dataInput <- eventReactive(input$load, {
  ...
})
```

(In that app the choices are named, `"rock" = 1`, so the server compares `input$dataset == 1`. With `choices = c("rock", "pressure", "cars")` you can keep your `switch()`.)
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Exercise 2 · Two buttons, two moments

In the live app above, add a second button `actionButton("draw", "Draw plot")` and make **only the plot** wait for it, while the summary updates as soon as the data are loaded.

*Hint*: you need a second `eventReactive()` that is triggered by `input$draw` and returns `dataInput()`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution 2

```r
# ui.R, in the sidebarPanel()
actionButton("draw", "Draw plot")
```

```r
# server.R
plotData <- eventReactive(input$draw, {
  dataInput()
})

output$graph <- renderPlot({
  data <- plotData()
  plot(data[, 1:2])
})
```

This is the idea of the next page: **one button to load the data, one to run the analysis**.
:::
